# US envoys head to Kyiv for first-ever visit after 'extremely frank' talks with Vladimir Putin
## Russia and Ukraine have agreed to a partial halt in strikes for three days so negotiations can continue.
5min read
Published 6 September 2026 9:47am
Source: AFP
Skip to article content

...

## In brief
* US envoys have proposed several ideas for how to end Russia's war with Ukraine in talks with Vladimir Putin.
* The envoys now head to Kyiv to meet with Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy.
**United States envoys proposed a "number of ideas" on how to end the Ukraine war in "frank" talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin late Saturday, Russian authorities said, ahead of the envoys' first trip to Kyiv.**
US President Donald Trump's business partner Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner met Putin for more than three hours, the Kremlin said, as Washington tries to revive negotiations to end Europe's worst conflict since World War Two.

...

## READ MORE
* The challenge brewing behind the front lines in Ukraine
Russia's TASS news agency reported that the Americans had flown out of Moscow.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said he was expecting the envoys on Sunday, and it was unclear how they would get to Kyiv by then.
Ukrainian airspace has been closed since Moscow launched the war in February 2022, and visiting leaders have been arriving by train.

## Putin thanks Trump
Early Sunday, Putin had thanked Trump for persisting in his efforts to end the war — launched by Russia in 2022 — despite it being "not simple".
Of the envoys' trip to Kyiv, he said: "No matter what happens next, contacts of this kind are undoubtedly always beneficial."

...

## Limited truce
Zelenskyy — who had offered a truce during the US visits — later said he had spoken to the US envoys and also promised Kyiv would not strike Moscow.
"From now through the end of Saturday, as well as on Sunday and Monday, Ukraine is ready to refrain from strikes on Moscow," Zelenskyy said.

...

## Russian strikes
As the US envoys were in the Kremlin, Ukraine said Russian attacks had killed three members of the same family in the city of Chuguiv in the north-eastern Kharkiv region.
"As a result of this shelling, almost the entire family was killed: a 19-year-old girl, an 11-year-old boy, and a 45-year-old man," regional leader Oleg Synegubov said.
Earlier Saturday, Russia struck Kyiv's suburbs and the Dnipro region, where local officials said five people had been killed.
Zelenskyy accused Moscow of trying to disrupt the visit of the US envoys with overnight attacks on Kyiv's two airports — as well as on civilian targets.

One late August strike **[demolished a major food distribution center](https://www.facebook.com/ukraineforchrist.org/posts/on-the-evening-of-august-28-the-enemy-destroyed-the-warehouse-and-office-of-our-/122195363294789935/)** , he adds, destroying “90 percent of the food distribution

infrastructure.
(Photo courtesy of SGA)

...

## Going local
“In the beginning of the war, we were assisting in shipping food via trucks from Poland and Germany; we helped out with over 115 truckloads full of aid,” Mock says.
“But as the war continued on, we shifted [our approach] to investing in local communities.”
Today, needs are increasing on the front lines. “Many of those communities are feeling the assault every single night, and now even every single day,” Mock says.
> **“Life for them is difficult, and access to basic human needs, especially with the winter months coming, is scarcer.”**

“When I was there last week in Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine, I think the one thing we talked about was the reality that life is fragile. We never know whether the Lord will grant us another day,” Mock says.
“So, given that life is that fragile, there’s a hunger for the Gospel, a hunger for knowing that the best is yet to come.”
Pray also for “the churches that are staying in the fight, as it were,” Mock adds. “These are the churches offering relief, the goodness of God, and the Gospel of Jesus Christ.”
